# Kyoto Spring Trip Plan for 2 Adults

A balanced 4-day Kyoto itinerary for **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-13** that fits **temples, gardens, local food, moderate walking**, and includes **one slower day**. The plan keeps the trip within a **$1,800 total budget excluding international flights** by using a mid-range hotel area and mostly transit-friendly sightseeing.

## Day-by-Day Kyoto Itinerary and Budget

### Day 1: Higashiyama Welcome Walk
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and settle near Kyoto Station or central Karasuma.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Kiyomizu-dera**, then stroll the preserved lanes of **Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka**.
- **Dinner:** Kaiseki-style set meal or a tempura/soba dinner in Gion.
- **Local transport:** **$12–$18** for 2 adults
- **Meals:** **$70–$110**
- **Why this works:** Classic Kyoto scenery with manageable walking and strong first-day energy.

### Day 2: Arashiyama Gardens and Riverside
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/tree.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Arashiyama Bamboo Grove** early, then **Tenryu-ji** garden.
- **Afternoon:** Slow riverside time near **Togetsukyo Bridge** and optional **Okochi Sanso Garden**.
- **Dinner:** Yudofu, tofu kaiseki, or a casual noodle dinner back in central Kyoto.
- **Local transport:** **$14–$22**
- **Meals:** **$70–$120**
- **Why this works:** Garden-focused day with scenic stops and moderate walking.

### Day 3: Slower Temple and Market Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/moon-stars.svg
- **Morning:** Start late with **Nishiki Market** for breakfast bites and local snacks.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/e5/A_store_at_Nishiki_market%2C_Kyoto%2C_Japan.jpg Alt=Morning:** Start late with **Nishiki Market** for breakfast bites and local snacks, Kyoto, Japan
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Nijo Castle** or **Kyoto Imperial Palace Park** at an easy pace.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ee/Shugaku-in_Imperial_Villa_-_Lower_Garden_a.JPG Alt=Afternoon:** Visit **Nijo Castle** or **Kyoto Imperial Palace Park** at an easy pace, Kyoto, Japan
- **Dinner:** Izakaya or Kyoto-style obanzai dinner.
- **Local transport:** **$10–$16**
- **Meals:** **$80–$130**
- **Why this works:** This is the **slower pace day** with fewer moves and more flexible timing.

### Day 4: Northern Kyoto Temples
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit **Kinkaku-ji** early to avoid crowds.
- **Afternoon:** Continue to **Ryoan-ji** and, if energy allows, **Ninna-ji**.
- **Dinner:** Final meal near Kyoto Station or downtown before departure.
- **Local transport:** **$14–$24**
- **Meals:** **$70–$120**
- **Why this works:** Strong temple finale with efficient routing and limited backtracking.

## Budget Breakdown and Stay Area

| Category | Estimated Total for 2 Adults | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Hotel, 3 nights | **$420–$720** | Mid-range business hotel or compact city hotel |
| Local transport | **$50–$80** | Subway, bus, and a few short taxi rides if needed |
| Meals | **$290–$480** | Mix of casual lunches, nicer dinners, snacks |
| Temple/garden entry | **$60–$120** | Depends on optional gardens and castle add-ons |
| Misc. buffer | **$120–$200** | Coffee, souvenirs, extra taxis, small extras |
| Total | **$940–$1,600** | Stays comfortably under your **$1,800** cap |

### Best Hotel Area to Stay
**Recommended area: Kyoto Station or central Karasuma/Shijo.**

- **Kyoto Station:** Best for easy airport/shinkansen access, luggage handling, and simple transit to Higashiyama, Arashiyama, and northern temples.
- **Karasuma/Shijo:** Best for restaurants, shopping, and a more central feel; also convenient for subway access.
- **Budget fit:** Look for a **3-star business hotel or compact boutique hotel** in these areas to keep nightly rates reasonable while staying well connected.

### Practical Fit for Your Priorities
- **Temples and gardens:** Strong coverage in Higashiyama, Arashiyama, and northern Kyoto.
- **Moderate walking:** Each day has one main cluster, avoiding overly spread-out sightseeing.
- **Local food:** Markets, tofu, obanzai, soba, and kaiseki-style dinners are built in.
- **Slower pace:** Day 3 is intentionally lighter and more flexible.
